title: The bound a set of prices proves

blocks.text: A city transit agency splits its maintenance money between buses, rail and ferries. Its analyst has no solver on the laptop she brings to the board meeting, but she wants to say, with proof, "no plan can be worth more than this". She has candidate prices for the rows and needs a function that says what bound they prove, if any.

The agency's LP, with $`A`$ the activities, $`R`$ the rows, $`v_j`$ the value per unit of activity $`j`$, $`a_{ij}`$ its coefficient in row $`i`$ (0 if it does not appear) and $`b_i`$ the row's right-hand side:
\max \sum_{j \in A} v_j\, x_j \quad \text{s.t.} \quad \sum_{j \in A} a_{ij}\, x_j \le b_i \;\; \forall i \in R, \qquad x_j \ge 0 \;\; \forall j \in A
Prices $`y_i`$ prove the bound $`\sum_{i \in R} b_i\, y_i`$ when every price is $`y_i \ge 0`$ and they cover every activity: $`\sum_{i \in R} a_{ij}\, y_i \ge v_j`$ for every $`j \in A`$.

Write `price_bound(value, rows, prices)` in `bound.py`. `value` maps each activity to $`v_j`$; `rows` maps each row's name to a pair `(coefficients, rhs)`, where `coefficients` maps the activities in that row to $`a_{ij}`$; `prices` maps every row's name to $`y_i`$. Return the bound the prices prove, or `None` when they prove nothing. Compare the cover sums with a tolerance of `1e-9`, since prices are floats.

"""Run executes this file. Change the calls and see what prints. Submit grades."""
import logging

# Turn the logger up, so the `log.debug` lines of your code show under the printed lines.
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")

from bound import price_bound

# A clinic's LP: hours on scans, tests and visits, value per hour.
value = {"scans": 0.6, "tests": 0.4, "visits": 0.2}
rows = {
    "staff": ({"scans": 1, "tests": 1, "visits": 1}, 500),
    "scanner": ({"scans": 1}, 150),
}
print("prices staff 0.6, scanner 0:", price_bound(value, rows, {"staff": 0.6, "scanner": 0.0}))
print("prices staff 0.4, scanner 0.2:", price_bound(value, rows, {"staff": 0.4, "scanner": 0.2}))
print("prices staff 0.3, scanner 0.3:", price_bound(value, rows, {"staff": 0.3, "scanner": 0.3}))
print("prices staff 0.7, scanner -0.1:", price_bound(value, rows, {"staff": 0.7, "scanner": -0.1}))

cases.says: prices that cover every activity's value prove their bound, and prices that leave one uncovered prove nothing
prices whose column sums equal an activity's value exactly still cover it
a negative price on a <= row makes the prices unusable, even if they cover every activity
an activity with a positive value that no row limits can never be covered
a row's price is weighted by the activity's coefficient in that row

origin.section: Any Nonnegative Prices on the Rows Give an Upper Bound

concepts: nonnegative prices that cover every variable's objective coefficient prove an upper bound on every plan
